sources.entry: litecli - SQLite CLI with autocompletion and syntax highlighting.

summary.one_liner: litecli is a command-line client for SQLite databases with auto-completion and syntax highlighting.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes litecli as a command-line client for SQLite databases that offers auto-completion and syntax highlighting. It is installed with pip (the README suggests the sqlean extra, pip install -U litecli[sqlean]) or with Homebrew on macOS. It is launched as litecli [OPTIONS] [DATABASE], with an example of passing a SQLite database file name. A config file is created automatically on first launch at ~/.config/litecli/config (or a path under AppData on Windows), and the README says the file documents all available options. Further feature details are pointed to on the project's docs site at litecli.com/features. The README itself is brief and does not list features beyond those above.
use_cases: query a SQLite database from the terminal
browse and edit local SQLite database files
autocomplete SQL keywords and table names while typing
inspect .sqlite or .db files with a friendlier shell
notable: Auto-completion for SQL in the terminal
Automatically creates a config file on first launch
caveats: The README gives little detail beyond installation and usage; features are documented on an external docs site
Installing on Linux may require sudo, per the README
